scope_allowed: Relevance of the quantities of interest

models.name: Defect-Resolved Cement Mantle Model (DR-CMM)
models.what_it_computes: Local time-dependent stresses and strains within a defect-bearing cement mantle using implicit FE with viscoelastic creep and cohesive interfaces to estimate crack initiation indices and creep accumulation.

models.name: Patient-Scale Cement Mantle Assembly Model (PS-CMAM)
models.what_it_computes: Global load transfer across stem–cement–bone with implicit FE using homogenized mantle properties and continuum damage to compute initiation risk metrics, interfacial shear, and creep-driven settlement.

mechanisms.name: Sustained axial loading–induced creep
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Time-dependent deformation of the cement mantle can reduce joint stability and alter load paths, contributing to loosening.

mechanisms.name: Bending fatigue–driven crack initiation at defects
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Repeated gait-like bending can nucleate cracks at pores and notches within the mantle, threatening structural integrity.

mechanisms.name: Torsional overload–assisted interfacial debond and radial cracking
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sudden twist events can elevate shear at interfaces, promoting debond and radial crack initiation that propagate under subsequent loading.

deviation.detail: All credibility factor scores are assigned on a 0–8 Credibility Readiness Level (CRL) scale for each model-by-mechanism pair.

expected_decision.outcome_source: Overall, DR-CMM attains CRL 6–7 for creep and bending initiation and CRL 5 for torsion, while PS-CMAM attains CRL 5–6 for creep and torsion and CRL 3–4 for bending initiation.

datasets: sustained axial creep under 37 C physiological conditions
notched-bar cyclic bending with micro-CT defect characterization
sudden torsional events using stem–cement–bone constructs
54 dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) tests spanning 0.1–10 Hz and 20–40 C
15 push-out and torsional shear tests using stem–cement and cement–bone coupons
18 stem–cement–bone stacks loaded at 1 kN in 37 C saline
shear-lag sensor readings at the locations probed
23 retrospective cases with RSA-measured migration reported in the literature at 6 and 12 months
acceptance_criteria: initiation was defined at the point where a 0.1 mm surface crack became visible in DIC at 20× magnification
categorizing above or below a 10 N·m criterion

Temperature was maintained at 37 ± 0.5 C using water-jacketed baths, relative humidity at 95 ± 3% using environmental chambers, load alignment within 0.3 deg, and waveform amplitudes within 2% of target values.

name_keywords: local creep strains near pores at 24 h
DIC measurements under 1 kN at 37 C
torque threshold for interfacial debond 12.0 ± 1.1 N·m
bending risk metric AUC 0.74 and 33% MAPE
torsional stiffness within 18% and onset metric r = 0.62
viscoelastic settlement correlated with 12-month RSA axial migration r = 0.68

findings.mechanism: Sustained axial loading–induced creep
spans: For sustained axial creep, DR-CMM predicted local creep strains near pores with 8.1% median absolute error at 24 h relative to DIC measurements on cement coupons under 1 kN compressive load and 37 C.

For small mantle segments, the model predicted 24 h settlement of 61 ± 9 micrometers compared to measured 56 ± 8 micrometers (9.3% absolute error on the mean), and matched the 7-day trend within 12.4% after time– temperature shift calibration.
findings.span: For sustained axial creep, DR-CMM predicted local creep strains near pores with 8.1% median absolute error at 24 h relative to DIC measurements on cement coupons under 1 kN compressive load and 37 C.

findings.mechanism: Bending fatigue–driven crack initiation at defects
spans: For bending fatigue, the model reproduced cycles to visible crack initiation at notches with a 21% median absolute percent error across 30 tests and captured the slope of the log–log S–N relation within 0.08 of the fitted experimental exponent.
Bending fatigue comparisons for DR-CMM involved 30 notched-bar tests.
findings.span: For bending fatigue, the model reproduced cycles to visible crack initiation at notches with a 21% median absolute percent error across 30 tests and captured the slope of the log–log S–N relation within 0.08 of the fitted experimental exponent.

findings.mechanism: Torsional overload–assisted interfacial debond and radial cracking
spans: Torsional overload comparisons used stem–cement–bone constructs with torque pulses of 10–20 N·m.
findings.span: Torsional overload comparisons used stem–cement–bone constructs with torque pulses of 10–20 N·m.

findings.mechanism: Torsional overload–assisted interfacial debond and radial cracking
spans: Interfaces with the stem and bone are represented by traction–separation cohesive laws with a mixed-mode Benzeggagh–Kenane (BK) criterion and rate dependence consistent with polymer interfacial behavior.

Assumptions and omissions were documented: temperature was held constant at 37 C post-cure; porosity was assumed stable over the time frames studied (no pore coalescence); hydration effects of saline immersion on PMMA were neglected based on literature indicating small volumetric changes over weeks; and frictional heating during torsional overload was not modeled, which we expect to slightly elevate the predicted torque threshold compared to cases where local softening from heat might occur.
findings.span: Interfaces with the stem and bone are represented by traction–separation cohesive laws with a mixed-mode Benzeggagh–Kenane (BK) criterion and rate dependence consistent with polymer interfacial behavior.

findings.mechanism: Sustained axial loading–induced creep
spans: Calibration involved fitting to DMA storage and loss moduli via nonlinear least squares, yielding E0 = 2.4 ± 0.3 GPa, a primary viscosity of 3.1 ± 0.8 GPa·s, and a secondary viscosity of 0.46 ± 0.12 GPa·s at 37 C.
findings.span: Calibration involved fitting to DMA storage and loss moduli via nonlinear least squares, yielding E0 = 2.4 ± 0.3 GPa, a primary viscosity of 3.1 ± 0.8 GPa·s, and a secondary viscosity of 0.46 ± 0.12 GPa·s at 37 C.

spans: Defect fields in DR-CMM were drawn from micro-CT reconstructions of 27 cement coupons, resulting in a pore volume fraction of 3.2 ± 1.1% and a median pore diameter of 120 micrometers (interquartile range 80–200 micrometers).

findings.mechanism: Bending fatigue–driven crack initiation at defects
spans: Bending fatigue tests used notched cement bars (3 × 6 × 60 mm) with notch radii 0.5 and 1.0 mm, tested in three-point bending at 0.5, 1, and 3 Hz to achieve nominal tensile stress amplitudes of 10, 20, and 30 MPa with R ratios of 0 and 0.5.

spans: Triangular torque pulses (up to 10, 12, 15, and 20 N·m) were applied over 0.3–0.5 s while monitoring torque, angle, and acoustic emissions.

findings.mechanism: Sustained axial loading–induced creep
spans: For sustained axial creep, 1000 LHS runs with shuffled seeds showed that the 24 h settlement’s variance was dominated by the primary dashpot viscosity (first-order Sobol index S1 = 0.58) and equilibrium modulus (S1 = 0.22), with negligible contributions from friction coefficients.
findings.span: For sustained axial creep, 1000 LHS runs with shuffled seeds showed that the 24 h settlement’s variance was dominated by the primary dashpot viscosity (first-order Sobol index S1 = 0.58) and equilibrium modulus (S1 = 0.22), with negligible contributions from friction coefficients.

findings.mechanism: Bending fatigue–driven crack initiation at defects
spans: For bending initiation, 1200 LHS runs on DR-CMM specimens with synthetic defect fields preserving the measured statistics revealed that the pore aspect ratio (S1 = 0.46) and maximum pore diameter (S1 = 0.27) were the primary drivers of cycles to first crack at 20 MPa amplitude, with viscoelastic parameters influencing hysteretic energy but not strongly shifting the initiation threshold.
findings.span: For bending initiation, 1200 LHS runs on DR-CMM specimens with synthetic defect fields preserving the measured statistics revealed that the pore aspect ratio (S1 = 0.46) and maximum pore diameter (S1 = 0.27) were the primary drivers of cycles to first crack at 20 MPa amplitude, with viscoelastic parameters influencing hysteretic energy but not strongly shifting the initiation threshold.

findings.mechanism: Torsional overload–assisted interfacial debond and radial cracking
spans: For torsional overload, 600 LHS runs indicated that interfacial shear strength (S1 = 0.63) and mixed-mode fracture energy (S1 = 0.19) set the torque threshold in DR-CMM, while friction coefficient played a minor role before debond onset.

findings.mechanism: Bending fatigue–driven crack initiation at defects
spans: For bending initiation, the model’s risk metric (a normalized damage-driving variable) ranked specimens by early crack likelihood with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.74 relative to whether a visible crack nucleated before 2 × 10^5 cycles, but the model did not localize microcrack sites absent defect resolution, with a 33% MAPE on cycles to first visible crack.

findings.mechanism: Torsional overload–assisted interfacial debond and radial cracking

findings.span: For torsional overload cases, PS-CMAM reproduced global torsional stiffness of the construct within 18% and predicted an onset metric correlated with measured debond thresholds with r = 0.62 over 12 specimens, resulting in a 24% MAPE for torque at initiation when a direct threshold was inferred from the metric calibration.
